subject: Re: CheckoutFlow order hold — persistent completion tails, exec alignment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@cartquick.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-12T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: CheckoutFlow order hold — large % of orders stalled in 'pending' (p99 spike)

Naomi,

We're seeing a recurring problem this morning where ~2.7% of CheckoutFlow requests are stalling in 'pending' for >30s. At 07:45 PT we had a sustained window where p99 jumped to 6.2s and a handful of orders stayed pending for 60-90s before completing. This is directly impacting conversions. Attached is a small sample of request traces and a tail snapshot (cartquick_samples.log).

Context: we haven't changed our integration. Traffic is up ~15% because of a promo; rate profile is more bursty than usual.

Can you confirm whether this is an issue on your side (queueing/backpressure) or something we need to change? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether this will count toward SLA credits.

- Samir
Head of Platform, CartQuick
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@cartquick.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-12T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CheckoutFlow order hold — large % of orders stalled in 'pending' (p99 spike)

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're on it. Immediate plan:
- Triage with SRE and serving engineers to confirm source (queueing vs model latency).
- If we confirm queue backpressure for your traffic slice, we'll put a short mitigation in (routing to a dedicated pool / lower concurrency cap) and roll it out as a canary.
- I'll escalate this to our Ops lead and schedule an exec sync at 14:00 PT to review impact and any crediting.

Expect a first update within 30 minutes.

Sorry for the hit — we know this is high priority.

Naomi Feldman
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CheckoutFlow order hold — initial triage notes

Quick notes from the first 20m:
- Observed p99 and p999 spikes correlated with a specific routing key for cartquick-production-us-west.
- Serving captures show many in-flight requests queued behind long-running requests (~>1.5s token generation each) that have larger context sizes than their median. This triggers larger KV cache churn and memory pressure for that pool.
- Concurrency cap for that pool is currently 96 concurrent streams; during bursts we hit the cap which activates internal request queueing and backpressure.
- Batching heuristic is misclassifying some small, latency-sensitive requests and waiting for batch windows; that increases head-of-line wait for others.

Short-term mitigation options (recommended order):
1) Temporarily reduce concurrency cap for cartquick slice to 64 and route overflow to a higher-capacity dedicated pool (if capacity available). This reduces queue depth and isolates long-tail requests.
2) Adjust batching config for cartquick routing key: set max_batch_delay_ms=5 (was 20) and lower batch_size_threshold for small requests.
3) Enable prefix-cache favoring for CheckoutFlow short requests to avoid repeated KV warmups.

I'll open SUP-4783 for tracking. Need Ops to approve routing change and capacity transfer.

- David (SRE)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-12T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CheckoutFlow order hold — batching heuristic regression suspected

Adding detail on the batching side: our recent heuristic update (rolled 10/05) introduced a change to 'batch wait sampling' that increases batch windows for traffic with sporadic large-context examples. CartQuick's promo increased variance and pushed more requests into a 'wait for batch' path. Result: artificially long batching windows for latency-sensitive flows.

Immediate hotfix I can roll in <15min:
- Revert the sampling tweak for the cartquick routing key only.
- Short-term override: max_batch_delay_ms=5, batch_size_threshold=6.

I'll prepare a canary with the override and push to 5% of CartQuick traffic first. If we see p99 fall, we will ramp to 100% and then consider a permanent heuristic revert with a follow-up perf test.

- Marcus (Serving Engineer)
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@cartquick.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@cartquick.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-12T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CheckoutFlow order hold — mitigation in progress

Samir — update: thanks for the trace set. Engineering has identified two correlated factors: batching heuristic behavior and capacity pressure (concurrency cap). We are deploying a canary with modified batching parameters and routing a slice to a higher-capacity pool.

Timeline: canary live within ~15 minutes; if green we'll ramp for the remainder of traffic and expect visible p99 improvements within 30 minutes of the ramp.

We will also offer a retroactive credit if the window constitutes an SLA impact — we'll confirm exact credit calculations at the 14:00 PT exec sync. Can you confirm you are available at 14:00 PT for a short cross-company call?

Attachments: initial-triage-notes.pdf (ops snapshot)

Naomi

- Samir
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-12T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Exec sync prep & next steps

Summary for the 14:00 PT exec sync:
- Impact: CartQuick saw p99 jump to 6.2s for a ~20m window; estimated 1.9-2.7% of sessions affected and several orders delayed 60-90s.
- Root cause (hypothesis): batching heuristic + concurrency cap hit → head-of-line queueing + KV cache churn.
- Immediate actions taken: canary with batching overrides rolled to 5% at 09:55 PT, routed overflow to dedicated pool at 10:05 PT. Observed p99 drop to ~1.4s on canary. Full ramp completed at 10:20 PT.
- Ask for exec sync: approve formal SLA credit formula (we will present calculations), confirm whether to provision a temporary dedicated capacity increase for peak windows during promos, and authorize a post-mortem with action owners.

Links: SUP-4783 (trouble ticket), PagerDuty incident PDT-12481, dashboard (shared). I'm prepping the postmortem template (postmortem-ops-template.md) and will capture timeline.

Marissa Cole
Head of Ops — Redwood Inference
